steps: Calculate the optical path difference introduced by the first slab: $\Delta x_1 = (\mu_1 - 1)t_1 = (1.5 - 1) \times 2 \text{ mm} = 1 \text{ mm}$.
Calculate the optical path difference introduced by the second slab: $\Delta x_2 = (\mu_2 - 1)t_2 = (1.4 - 1) \times 1.5 \text{ mm} = 0.6 \text{ mm}$.
Find the net path difference at the center of the screen: $\Delta x = |\Delta x_1 - \Delta x_2| = 1 \text{ mm} - 0.6 \text{ mm} = 0.4 \text{ mm}$.
Use the formula for the shift of the central maxima: $y = \Delta x \frac{D}{d}$.
Substitute the given values ($D = 1 \text{ m}$, $d = 5 \text{ mm}$): $y = 0.4 \text{ mm} \times \frac{1 \text{ m}}{5 \text{ mm}} = 0.08 \text{ m}$.
Convert the shift to cm: $y = 0.08 \text{ m} = 8 \text{ cm}$.
